name: Apus
introduction: is the Bird of Paradise, introduced by Dutch navigators in the 1590s. Its name means “footless”, because birds of paradise arrived in Europe as skins without feet. It lies near the south celestial pole.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Because traders removed the feet from bird-of-paradise skins before shipping them from New Guinea, European naturalists believed the birds never landed and spent their whole lives in the air. The constellation preserves that legend.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Paradys](hip:72370), Alpha Apodis, is an orange giant. [Gamma Apodis](hip:81065) and [Beta Apodis](hip:81852) are orange and yellow giants.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The globular clusters NGC 6101 and IC 4499 lie in Apus, far out in the halo of the Milky Way.
